decisions.question: Which provider-neutral authentication and session approach will Kairo V1 use?
options: Managed standards-based OIDC/OAuth provider
Self-hosted standards-based identity
Another standards-based approach approved by ADR
decisions.decision: Use a managed standards-based OIDC/OAuth provider behind a Kairo-owned provider-neutral identity/session adapter. Provider-specific SDKs and configuration remain outside the domain boundary; Kairo remains authoritative for Workspace/Brand membership, authorization and audit.
decisions.rationale: This minimizes the V1 identity security surface while preserving standards and provider replaceability. It also keeps tenant authorization in Kairo-owned records rather than coupling product policy to one identity vendor.

decisions.question: Which lightweight TypeScript API framework will implement the approved modular API boundary?
options: Fastify
Equivalent lightweight TypeScript framework approved by ADR
decisions.decision: Use Fastify for the Kairo V1 TypeScript modular API transport layer, with domain/application modules independent of Fastify-specific types.
decisions.rationale: Fastify matches the approved lightweight TypeScript API direction, supports schema-driven validation and OpenAPI, and can remain confined to the transport adapter boundary.

decisions.question: Which semantic retrieval provider is promoted after the representative Brand-memory benchmark?
options: Qdrant with TurboQuant
PgVector fallback
decisions.decision: Promote PgVector as Kairo V1 semantic retrieval for Hunter coverage/novelty memory and other V1 semantic lookups, behind the provider-neutral semantic retrieval boundary. PostgreSQL remains authoritative domain truth. Keep Qdrant with TurboQuant as the scale-up candidate to re-benchmark when corpus size, latency, concurrency or memory pressure justifies promotion.
decisions.rationale: The corrected fail-closed VS-03 benchmark gave both providers recall@10 of 1.0 and zero tenant leaks on the representative 7,200-vector multi-Brand surrogate. Tuned PgVector delivered lower V1 query latency and avoids a second operational datastore for the current daily Hunter/coverage-memory workload. The provider-neutral boundary preserves a later Qdrant/TurboQuant migration without moving authoritative business truth.

decisions.question: What publishing mode is approved for Instagram and LinkedIn after exact V1 API feasibility is verified?
options: Automated adapters for both channels
Automated adapter for one channel with manual fallback for the other
Manual publishing for unsupported pilot channel paths
decisions.decision: Implement official deterministic automated publishing adapters for Instagram Professional accounts and LinkedIn organization Pages. Enable each connection only after capability and permission verification; use an explicit manual publishing workflow whenever platform review, account type, role, content type or API capability is unavailable. Scheduling remains Kairo-owned and only approved immutable Content Versions may be dispatched.
decisions.rationale: Meta officially supports content publishing for Instagram Professional accounts and LinkedIn's versioned Posts API supports organization posting with w_organization_social. Both require OAuth consent, appropriate account/Page roles and platform-granted access; therefore capability-gated automation plus a first-class manual fallback is the reliable V1 mode.

decisions.question: How should Kairo use Agent Reach for public discovery and research?
options: Adopt Agent Reach as a replaceable Dynamic Skill and DiscoverySourceProvider behind Kairo ToolGateway
Call Agent Reach directly from Hermes with unrestricted shell access
Do not use Agent Reach
decisions.decision: Adopt Agent Reach as a replaceable Dynamic Skill and DiscoverySourceProvider behind Kairo-owned ToolGateway. Pin and evaluate an approved upstream revision; Hermes may invoke only Kairo-scoped capabilities, never unrestricted Agent Reach shell access. Kairo remains authoritative for Brand isolation, permissions, provenance, normalization, secrets, budgets, policy and stored domain state.
decisions.rationale: Agent Reach provides useful multi-source public discovery across web, RSS, YouTube, GitHub and configurable social sources while preserving Kairo's architecture if it is wrapped behind a provider boundary. Direct unrestricted agent execution would weaken tenant isolation, auditability, provenance and secret controls. The provider remains replaceable and source-specific official APIs may supersede it where required.

decisions.question: What deletion propagation policy applies when a private Brand knowledge source is removed or replaced?
options: Delete raw source and source-only derived retrieval data; retain content-free audit tombstone; preserve user-confirmed facts; mark unsupported AI-inferred facts stale until reconfirmed or re-supported
Delete all derived Brand Brain facts including user-confirmed facts
Retain derived private memory after the source is removed
decisions.decision: Delete raw private source content and source-only derived retrieval data; retain only a content-free audit tombstone; preserve user-confirmed facts as independent authoritative Brand Brain input; mark AI-inferred facts stale when they lose all active supporting sources until reconfirmed or re-supported; replacement creates new provenance/version links rather than silently mutating historical evidence.
decisions.rationale: This makes source removal meaningful for privacy and retrieval while preserving user-confirmed Brand facts whose authority no longer depends on the deleted source. It also prevents stale unsupported inferences from continuing to influence Kairo as authoritative context.

decisions.question: How should Kairo treat OpenReply for Instagram engagement and conversion automation?
options: Keep OpenReply as a deferred reference/evaluation candidate for a future deterministic Instagram EngagementAutomationAdapter
Adopt OpenReply as a V1 core dependency
Run OpenReply as an unrestricted Dynamic Skill
decisions.decision: Keep OpenReply as a deferred, non-V1 reference and evaluation candidate for future Instagram engagement/conversion automation. If later promoted, reuse or adapt only the useful deterministic patterns behind Kairo-owned channel/engagement ports, including comment-to-DM, tracked-link attribution, rate limiting, webhook handling and engagement outcome capture. Do not adopt OpenReply's separate Workspace/auth model, Redis/BullMQ requirement, inbox/community-management surface or direct credentials as Kairo Core dependencies. Dynamic Skills may recommend an engagement strategy, but deterministic Kairo adapters must execute social actions and retain credentials, idempotency, audit and outcome state.
decisions.rationale: OpenReply demonstrates useful official-Meta-API patterns that could later strengthen Kairo's conversion and Performance Memory loop, but its current product/runtime model overlaps Kairo-owned tenancy and operational concerns and includes capabilities explicitly outside V1. Deferring it preserves current scope while keeping a valuable implementation reference available for a later engagement/conversion phase.

decisions.question: Which pilot deployment topology and providers should host the certified Kairo V1 release?
options: Split topology: managed Next.js frontend + container API + managed PostgreSQL
Single-provider topology with compatible Next.js, container/API and PostgreSQL capabilities
Another provider-neutral topology supported by current official capability, pricing and operational evidence
decisions.decision: Use a split non-production pilot topology: Vercel Hobby for the Next.js web application, Render Free Web Service in Frankfurt for the containerized Node.js/Fastify API, and Neon Free Postgres in AWS Europe (Frankfurt) with pgvector. Keep provider boundaries and exact-SHA release provenance. Before commercial use or production enablement, reassess and approve paid plans appropriate to the workload; Vercel Hobby is non-commercial and Render Free is not approved by Render for production applications.
decisions.rationale: This matches Kairo's current pilot profile: non-commercial use, zero-dollar monthly target, low traffic, accepted cold starts, Next.js previews, container API, PostgreSQL with pooling, and no PITR requirement. Vercel is the strongest fit for the existing Next.js frontend; Render supports Docker web services and Frankfurt deployment; Neon provides persistent serverless Postgres in Frankfurt and supports Postgres 18 with pgvector. The free tiers satisfy the bounded non-production pilot constraints without coupling Kairo domain boundaries to any provider. Production enablement remains a separate exact-SHA human gate and must include a plan/capacity reassessment.

decisions.question: Which public discovery provider and credential boundaries are approved for the free-source Hunter expansion?
options: Official/public provider APIs and approved RSS/Atom feeds behind Kairo-owned adapters, with optional secret-scoped YouTube API key
Third-party aggregation/search SaaS for all discovery sources
Unrestricted scraping, browser sessions or user-cookie based discovery
decisions.decision: Use official/public discovery interfaces only: approved RSS/Atom feeds, the official Hacker News v0 API, Bluesky public AppView endpoints, and the YouTube Data API. Each provider stays behind a Kairo-owned DiscoverySourceProvider/ToolGateway boundary with deterministic request ceilings, timeouts, provenance, normalization and provider-isolated failure. YouTube credentials are optional infrastructure secrets resolved outside agent/domain context; when absent or quota-exhausted, the adapter disables/degrades without failing the Hunter. Do not use unrestricted scraping, browser cookies, private sessions or agent-visible provider credentials.
decisions.rationale: This implements the approved zero-subscription public-signal strategy while preserving provider replaceability, auditability and Brand isolation. Hacker News and Bluesky provide public unauthenticated reads; RSS/Atom is feed-driven; YouTube requires an API key and quota controls, so its credential must remain outside prompts and domain state. Provider failures must not collapse a multi-source Hunter run.

decisions.question: Should Kairo create a separate Business Intelligence feature or connect existing Brand Brain, Hunter/Research and Performance Learning through one shared Brand Memory layer?
options: Create a separate Business Intelligence page and parallel intelligence model
Use one shared Brand Memory/intelligence layer across existing Kairo workflows
decisions.decision: Do not create a separate Business Intelligence feature, page or parallel source of truth. Treat Brand Brain facts, active knowledge and channel sources, accepted Performance Memory, current Brand priorities and evidence-linked learnings as one shared Brand-scoped memory/intelligence layer. Onboarding initializes that layer; Hunter, Research, My Idea/Create, content strategy and Performance should consume the same approved Brand context through Kairo-owned application contracts. User-confirmed facts remain authoritative, learned signals remain evidence-linked, and only accepted Learnings may influence later recommendations. No workflow may silently overwrite confirmed Brand facts or read another Brand's private intelligence.
decisions.rationale: Kairo already implements the major intelligence components separately. Connecting them avoids duplicate UI and data models, strengthens the closed learning loop, and focuses differentiation on the quality of the next Brand decision rather than adding another dashboard.

decisions.question: Should authenticated social-channel connection remain inside Brand onboarding or happen after Kairo has learned the Brand from one public reference?
options: Require Website/social connection choices during onboarding
Start from one public URL and move authenticated channel connection to Home/Brand after onboarding
decisions.decision: Brand onboarding accepts one supported public HTTP(S) URL, lets Kairo infer Brand identity, audience, voice, positioning, content direction and provisional goals from evidence, shows a concise confirmation, and then enters Home. A public social URL is evidence only and grants no publishing, private Insights or authenticated channel authority. OAuth/channel connection moves after onboarding to Home Needs Attention and Brand connection surfaces; publishing and provider Insights still require the existing capability-checked authenticated connection. Existing channel adapters, scopes, tenant isolation and human publishing approval remain unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Channel authentication is not required to understand enough about a Brand to deliver first value. Moving OAuth after first value removes setup complexity without weakening publishing or data-access controls, and preserves one shared Brand Memory rather than coupling onboarding to provider workflows.

decisions.question: How should Kairo persist and execute optional Brand Avatar / Presenter functionality without coupling domain state, tenancy, credentials or publishing authority to one media provider?
options: Kairo-owned Presenter state plus replaceable AvatarProvider
Provider-owned Presenter profile
Frontend-only Presenter preferences until provider work arrives
decisions.decision: Use a Kairo-owned, Brand-scoped PresenterProfile as authoritative PostgreSQL state, private S3-compatible storage for reference/generated media, and a replaceable server-side AvatarProvider capability boundary. Provider SDKs, credentials and endpoint details remain outside domain/web code. Presenter eligibility fails closed unless the saved profile and configured provider binding are healthy. Generated presenter media enters normal immutable Content/Asset Version lineage before exact Preview and human approval; deterministic publishing receives only the exact approved final asset.
decisions.rationale: This follows the approved TRD dependency rules, preserves Workspace/Brand isolation and private-media policy, keeps providers replaceable, avoids fake frontend readiness, and retains exact asset/version approval and publishing guarantees.
